propositions: The reconciler unconditionally advances the cursor to the newest event timestamp in each pass, permanently dropping any candidate that fails to vote in that first pass, violating the contract that abandoned candidates are retried on the next pass.

Gerrit's webhooks plugin delivers at-most-once (not at-least-once as documented), discarding events on maxTries exceeded and on container recreation, making the reconciler the sole recovery path for dropped uploads.

A patch-set upload that times out or errors during review in pass N is never re-scanned in pass N+1 because the cursor already advanced past its event timestamp, and the server-side ?t1= filter (inclusive lower bound) excludes it forever.

The test suite's mock events-log ignores the since parameter and returns the full list regardless, masking the production bug where a failed review permanently disappears from the reconciler's window.

Multiple distinct manual nudges (recheck-review comment and no-op rebase) revive stalled changes by minting new events-log entries with timestamps after the cursor, proving the review is dropped-on-event not queued-in-worker.

The three operational states (bot down, review running, queued-behind-N, permanently-dropped) are not currently observable, preventing agents from diagnosing whether a stalled change is transient or permanent.
